html:
Adam Mickiewicz was the greatest poet of Polish Romanticism, born in 1798 near Navahrudak in today's Belarus, then in the former Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

He studied at Vilnius and was exiled to Russia in 1824 for joining a secret student society. After the failed November Uprising he lived in Paris among the Polish exiles. There he wrote Pan Tadeusz, of 1834, an epic of gentry life in Lithuania that opens "Lithuania, my fatherland" and is still the national poem of Poland. His drama Forefathers' Eve was banned by communist censors in 1968, sparking student protests. He died in Constantinople in 1855 while raising a legion to fight Russia. Belarus and Lithuania also honour him.
sum: Adam Mickiewicz was the greatest poet of Polish Romanticism, born in 1798 near Navahrudak in today's Belarus, then in the former Grand Duchy of Lithuania.
